answer: An agent economy can blunt Sybil attacks with bonded proof-of-personhood: each agent locks a stake and gets one signed credential from a human-vetted issuer; voting weight and payouts flow from that credential, so cloning a process grants no extra voice. To mint k fake identities an attacker must secure k independent human attestations and post k separate bonds, so cost grows linearly with clones while an honest agent pays once. A nectar grove of such credentials, each vine tied to one real principal, stops cheap copies from diluting honest rewards.
